note: Four proposed additions, written to Convergent's house format and kept in new_gaps so they are never mixed with theirs. Each cleared a dedup grep over all 103 gaps and all 369 capabilities, and a funding check against current programmes. A fifth candidate — queue and turnaround time at shared nanofabrication user facilities — was dropped: see the decision ledger.

gaps.name: Coating Thermal Noise Sets the Sensitivity Floor for Precision Optical Instruments
gaps.description: The mechanical loss of dielectric mirror coatings sets a Brownian noise floor that limits gravitational wave detectors, optical clocks and cavity-stabilised lasers alike. Coating development is pursued as a subsystem of each instrument rather than as a materials problem, so improvements arrive slowly and transfer poorly between instrument classes. Lower-loss coatings that can be deposited at metre scale are needed.
gaps.outcome: A whole class of precision instruments gains sensitivity at once rather than one at a time, and third-generation gravitational wave detectors reach their design sensitivity in the band where they are most useful.
gaps.tension_test: Wide agreement that the goal is transformative: the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer design cases both state that coating thermal noise limits sensitivity in the most sensitive frequency band, and ET's coatings programme describes minimal-noise coatings as essential to reaching expected sensitivity. Genuine debate about near-term feasibility: amorphous coatings have resisted large loss-angle reductions for two decades, crystalline AlGaAs and mixed TiO2:GeO2 candidates each have unresolved problems at metre-scale deposition, and there is no consensus on whether the required loss angle is reachable at all in an amorphous material. That is the tension: agreement on the prize, no agreement on whether it is available.
gaps.unlock_test: The dominoes are unusually well aligned because the quantity is shared. A lower loss angle improves gravitational wave detector reach directly; it also improves optical cavity stability, which sets the short-term stability of the best optical clocks, which in turn sets the sensitivity of clock-based tests of fundamental physics and of relativistic geodesy. Convergent's own Astrophysics gaps on gravitational wave frequency coverage and on formation flying both sit downstream of coating performance without naming it.
gaps.dedup_check: Grepped all 103 gaps and all 369 capabilities on /coating|thermal noise|mechanical loss|gravitational wave|interferomet|precision measurement|noise floor/. Two gaps matched, both Astrophysics: 'Limited Detection of Gravitational Waves Across the Frequency Spectrum', which is about extending detection to bands outside the audio band and whose three capabilities are space-based, decihertz and high-frequency detection; and 'Higher-Resolution Views of the Universe Are Roadblocked by Formation Flying Technology', which is about sub-micron spacecraft station-keeping. Five capabilities matched, none about coatings or mirror materials. The four Materials Science gaps cover discovery search, crystallization, scalable macroscale synthesis and element acquisition. Closest match overall is the gravitational wave frequency gap; it is distinct because frequency coverage and in-band sensitivity are different axes and a perfect coating does nothing for the first.
gaps.funding_check: Not clear of funding, and the honest version matters more than a clean answer. The NSF has funded the LSC Center for Coatings Research since 2017 (award 1707868, renewed as 2429369), whose stated premise is that 'the A+ upgrade and all 3rd generation detector designs depend on the development of mirrors with low coating thermal noise'. Italy's ETIC project funds coatings work for the Einstein Telescope through INFN, INAF and the universities of Padua and Bologna, testing mixed titanium and silicon dioxide films. Both are funded as detector subsystems inside one instrument programme. What is not funded anywhere found is the cross-instrument materials problem: no programme treats low-mechanical-loss optical coatings as a materials target in its own right, with the result that optical clock and cavity groups re-derive the same materials work. The gap proposed here is that framing, not the existence of coatings research, and it is stated that way deliberately.
gaps.rationale: Chosen as the safe case: unambiguous metric (coating loss angle, and coating thermal noise in the detector band), a concrete mid-scale build, and a large downstream unlock. It is tier 1 on their own roadmapping criterion, which is why it is offered first.
gaps.nearest: Closest is your Astrophysics gap “Limited Detection of Gravitational Waves Across the Frequency Spectrum”. It is about extending detection into new frequency bands; this is about sensitivity inside the band you already cover, which a perfect coating improves and a new band does not.

gaps.name: There Is No Machine-Readable Record of What Did Not Work
gaps.description: Negative results, null findings, abandoned approaches and rejected proposals are largely missing from the scientific record, and where they are captured the formats are neither standardised nor machine-readable. Systems that could learn from failure have little to learn from. Building this record requires shared formats and credit arrangements that no institution currently owns.
gaps.outcome: The failed half of the scientific record becomes available to both people and models, so an approach that has already been tried and abandoned can be recognised as such before it is funded again.
gaps.tension_test: Wide agreement that the goal is transformative: publication bias is one of the oldest and best-documented pathologies in metascience, and 2025 saw a values-based framework for surfacing null results published in PLOS Biology. Genuine debate about feasibility: every previous attempt at a negative-results journal or database has struggled, because the cost of depositing falls on the author and the benefit accrues to everyone else. The debate is not about whether the record would be useful, it is about whether any credit arrangement can make depositing rational for the person who has to do it.
gaps.unlock_test: Downstream of this sit three of Convergent's own metascience gaps. Literature synthesis at scale is synthesising a censored corpus. Fraud detection is easier when the distribution of real null results is known, because implausible cleanliness is what detection methods look for. Clinical trial optimisation depends on knowing which designs have already failed. It also acts on the materials and chemistry gaps: their own 'Open Synthesis Database' capability asks for procedure logs including failed experiments, which is this gap restricted to one field.
gaps.dedup_check: Grepped all 103 gaps and all 369 capabilities on /negative result|null result|failed experiment|unpublished|rejected proposal|reproducib|replicat|preregist|machine-readable|data sharing/. Six gaps matched, none about the missing record: they are about synthetic olfaction, manual chemical synthesis, manual bioengineering, evolved computation, superconductivity noise, and ephemeral platform data. Convergent's five metascience gaps cover fraud, synthesis at scale, publishing cost, clinical trial design and organisational rigidity, and none covers this. The closest match in the whole export is a capability, not a gap: 'Open Synthesis Database', attached to the Chemistry gap 'Limited Understanding of the Chemical Reaction Space', which asks for 'procedure logs and outcomes including failed experiments'. That is the same idea scoped to materials synthesis. The proposal here is that it generalises, and that generalising it is the gap.
gaps.funding_check: Initiatives exist and none is infrastructure. The Null Hypothesis Initiative and its Null Compass tool are running; ICPC and other venues run replication-and-negative-results tracks; Open Grants (ogrants.org) collects funded and unfunded proposals voluntarily; NegResCo built a COVID-specific negative results collection on ELIXIR platforms. Reporting on these efforts is consistent that they lack coordination and that data formats are not standardised. On the proposal side, the case for releasing unfunded applications is argued in Issues in Science and Technology and an OpenProposal platform was proposed in a 2025 preprint; no funder has implemented it. Nothing found is a funded, cross-field, machine-readable record under construction.
gaps.rationale: Proposed at tier 3 in effect and labelled Proxy only rather than dressed up: deposited records are countable, but the quantity that matters is the share of failures captured, and that denominator is unobservable by construction. Their own roadmapping criterion asks whether success is unambiguously measurable, and for this gap the honest answer is no. The audit in Phase 2 found Proxy only to be the least reliable tier in the taxonomy, which is a caveat on this label rather than on the gap.
gaps.nearest: Closest is not a gap but a capability: “Open Synthesis Database”, attached to your Chemistry gap “Limited Understanding of the Chemical Reaction Space”, which asks for procedure logs including failed experiments. That is this idea scoped to materials synthesis. The proposal is that it generalises, and that generalising it is the gap.

gaps.name: Survey Astronomy Is Limited by Simulation Fidelity More Than by Data Volume
gaps.description: Wide-field surveys now gather more data than their forward models can interpret. Constraints from imaging surveys and from microwave background experiments are increasingly set by the accuracy of simulated skies, instrument models and foreground models rather than by statistical precision. Simulation and emulator fidelity is becoming the limiting instrument.
gaps.outcome: The constraining power already sitting in Rubin and CMB-S4 data becomes recoverable, so a decade of survey operations converts into cosmological constraints rather than into systematic error budgets.
gaps.tension_test: Wide agreement that the goal is transformative: the CMB-S4 foreground-cleaning pipeline comparison reports biases at the 1-2 sigma level once realistic foreground complexity is included, and concludes that mutual validation of independent pipelines is essential to any claimed detection — an explicit statement that modelling, not noise, bounds the result. Genuine debate about feasibility: neural emulators reach percent-level accuracy on matter power spectra but their behaviour outside training distributions is exactly the regime that matters for systematics, and there is no agreement on how an emulator's error budget should be validated against the thing it replaces.
gaps.unlock_test: This is a rate limit shared across every survey facility now being built or commissioned, which is what makes it worth roadmapping rather than a per-experiment engineering task. Rubin, CMB-S4, Roman, DESI and Euclid all convert photons into parameters through the same kind of forward model. Improving that stage improves all of them, and it is the only stage where a decade of already-funded observing time can be made more valuable without new hardware. It also sits directly downstream of Convergent's telescope gap: an instrument that took thirty years to build is worth more if its data can be fully interpreted.
gaps.dedup_check: Grepped all 103 gaps and all 369 capabilities on /simulation|forward model|emulator|mock catalog|survey|systematic uncertaint|calibration/. Five gaps matched: mechanical systems modelling, civic engagement platforms, social science tooling, in-silico molecular simulation, and brain model systems. None is astrophysics. Fourteen capabilities matched; the nearest, 'Combine Physics Models and Generative AI', is attached to the Mechanical Engineering gap 'Sim-to-Real Transfer for Robots is Hard', and 'Modernize Survey Infrastructure' is a Social Science capability about human surveys, not sky surveys. Convergent's four Astrophysics gaps are telescope cost and schedule, unrealized planetary missions, gravitational wave frequency coverage, and formation flying. The closest genuine analogue anywhere in the export is the Chemistry gap 'In-Silico Molecular Simulation Is Slow and Kludgy', which is the same shape of problem in a different domain; that this map already contains that gap and not this one is the argument for adding it.
gaps.funding_check: Funded as project work inside each collaboration, not as a gap. LSST DESC maintains the DC2 simulated sky survey and a science roadmap that names required fidelity; CMB-S4 funds pipeline comparison studies; emulator development appears across individual grants and a 2026 Perimeter programme on field-level and simulation-based inference. All of it is scoped to one experiment's analysis. No programme found funds forward-model fidelity as a shared instrument across surveys, which is the level at which the work would transfer.
gaps.rationale: Included because the maturity label is 'Working now' and the gap is still open, which is the more interesting shape: this is not a case of AI being immature, it is a case of a capability that works being applied one collaboration at a time. Directly measurable because the ratio of systematic to statistical error in a published constraint is a number that both communities already report.
gaps.nearest: Closest anywhere in the export is your Chemistry gap “In-Silico Molecular Simulation Is Slow and Kludgy” — the same shape of problem in a different domain. None of your four Astrophysics gaps is about simulation, and the nearest capability, “Combine Physics Models and Generative AI”, is attached to a robotics sim-to-real gap.

gaps.name: Decision Latency for Large Scientific Facilities Is Not Treated as a Technical Problem
gaps.description: The elapsed time from a facility concept to first operation is dominated by review, ranking, authorisation and funding steps rather than by fabrication. These steps are studied as science policy and are rarely engineered. Methods that shorten decision cycles without weakening scrutiny would act on the same constraint across astronomy, particle physics and light sources.
gaps.outcome: The decades-long wait between a facility being conceived and being used shortens without anyone lowering the standard of scrutiny, which changes what a single scientific career can contain.
gaps.tension_test: Wide agreement that the goal is transformative: STScI states that JWST took 32 years from conception to launch, Rubin's own history runs from early-1990s planning to 2025 first light, and the Future Circular Collider debate turns explicitly on decisions having to be taken decades before operation. Genuine debate about feasibility: every proposed acceleration is suspected of being a reduction in scrutiny, and the one serious mechanism change in this space — distributed peer review at ESO and NOIRLab — is still argued about. That is a real tension rather than a rhetorical one, because the objection is legitimate.
gaps.unlock_test: The unlock is unusually broad because the constraint is shared rather than analogous. Astronomy, particle physics, light sources and neutron sources all run the same concept-to-operation pipeline, and all of them pass through proposal review at both the facility-approval and the observing-time stages. Convergent's own telescope gap is one instance of it, and their capability set for that gap — modular assembly, commercial components, a telescope factory — acts entirely on fabrication, which is downstream of the step this gap names. Shortening decision cycles also compounds: a facility approved five years earlier produces five more years of data.
gaps.dedup_check: Grepped all 103 gaps on the same fabrication and access patterns used above, and read all five Metascience gaps and all four Astrophysics gaps in full. Two near-misses, both real. 'Frontier Telescopes Are Expensive and Take Decades to Build' names the elapsed time and closes on needing 'the organizational structure and hunger to adopt such methods', but it is scoped to space telescopes and its capabilities are all build-side. 'A Limited Set of Rigid Organizational Structures for Organizing and Funding Research Constrains the Forms of R&D That Get Done' is about incentive structures and researcher time, not about elapsed time to a decision. This gap is the intersection they leave open: the elapsed-time axis, generalised past space telescopes, located in the approval mechanism rather than in build technology. It is offered as a completion of a sentence their telescope gap already starts.
gaps.funding_check: No programme found funds this. UKRI's Infrastructure Fund, Horizon Europe's Research Infrastructures work programme and NWO's large-scale research infrastructure route all fund the facilities themselves and their strategic prioritisation; none funds work on shortening the decision cycle. The one live mechanism experiment is distributed peer review, introduced by ESO at Period 110 for proposals below a time threshold, with each qualifying PI reviewing ten proposals, and previously deployed at ALMA and in Gemini's Fast Turnaround channel. ESO's own stated reasons are that panel load 'has become unsustainable', that triage 'has significantly degraded the quality of feedback', and that 'it has become progressively harder to find scientists willing to serve'. That is an observatory changing its review machinery under load, run at scale, with a before and after — and nobody is funding it as research.
gaps.rationale: The most speculative of the four on the AI axis and labelled so: no current capability acts on institutional decision latency, and claiming otherwise would be the kind of overreach this project is trying to avoid. Directly measurable nonetheless, because concept-to-first-light elapsed time is published for every major facility. Included because Phase 5 finds the same binding link independently from two different fields, which is a stronger reason to propose a gap than intuition is.
gaps.nearest: Two near-misses, both real. Your telescope gap names the elapsed time and closes on organisational structure, but is scoped to space telescopes with build-side capabilities only. Your rigid-organisational-structures gap is about incentives and researcher time, not elapsed time to a decision. This is the intersection they leave open.
